findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued is a shared import-time datetime and is not task-serializable
findings.body: AssignmentSource.queued uses timezone.now() as a dataclass default, which is evaluated once at import, so every source shares one timestamp instead of the time the webhook was handled. to_dict() then puts that datetime into assignment_source_dict, which sync_group_assignee_outbound passes as Celery kwargs. A datetime is not a JSON-safe payload; if the integrations queue serializes as JSON, apply_async raises and no outbound assignee task is enqueued. That drops sync to other integrations (the path this PR still wants) and can 500 the inbound webhook. from_dict also fail-opens: any TypeError/ValueError returns None, should_sync treats that as "no source", and the same-integration echo this PR is meant to stop is sent anyway. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) and serialize queued to an ISO string (and parse it in from_dict) before enqueueing.

findings.title: Outbound assignee sync always passes a new keyword implementations may not accept
findings.body: sync_assignee_outbound now always calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), including when the source is None. Previously this keyword was never passed. The abstract method accepts **kwargs, but concrete installations that declare (external_issue, user, assign=True) without **kwargs or assignment_source will raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync, then retry up to 5 times. That breaks assignee propagation for those providers, not only the cycle-break path. Confirm every sync_assignee_outbound implementation accepts the keyword, or only forward it when the implementation supports it.
